items.title: Welcome by the School Board President
First of Two Public Hearings: School Attendance Boundary Change for Neighborhood Schools

publicComments.name: Kathryn Stewart
publicComments.summary: Proposed a radical statewide lottery system for school assignment with pooled funding, eliminating the worst schools and modeling them after the best.

publicComments.name: Roberta Land
publicComments.summary: Expressed strong opposition to her Kentfield Commons neighborhood being assigned to Garfield, arguing it is not a neighborhood school and the route is dangerous for children.

publicComments.name: Katherine Hagman
publicComments.summary: Voiced strong support for Scenario 2, arguing it keeps the Mount Carmel neighborhood together and that the route to Clifford is safer for children than other options.

publicComments.name: Megan Maxwell Bay
publicComments.summary: Asked whether students currently attending a school of choice would be grandfathered in and allowed to remain at their existing school under boundary changes.

publicComments.name: Michelle Smith
publicComments.summary: Expressed concern about the lack of demographic data in the presentation, urging the board to consider equity and avoid de facto segregation when drawing boundaries.

publicComments.name: Meredith Park
publicComments.summary: Advocated strongly for walkable neighborhood schools and critiqued the school of choice model for fracturing neighborhood communities, noting her street's children attended 12 different schools despite all ending up together at Sequoia High.

publicComments.name: Cameron Matthews
publicComments.summary: Asked about population trend methodology behind the 2026 projections, requested walkability analysis tools for boundary fringe areas, and inquired whether additional scenario options beyond Scenarios 1 and 2 would be presented before the board vote.

publicComments.name: David Knox
publicComments.summary: Asked for clarification on whether students currently in the Roy Cloud boundary would be reassigned to another school under the proposed scenarios and whether grandfathering would apply.

publicComments.name: Eurydia Aquino
publicComments.summary: Asked whether her children, who attend RCSD schools via inter-district transfer while she works in the district, would be displaced or need to reapply under boundary changes.

publicComments.name: Annie and Andreas Hildebrandt
publicComments.summary: Expressed strong support for Scenario 2, sharing that their son moved from private school to Roy Cloud and found community, and that neighbors would also enroll in public school under that scenario.

publicComments.name: Stephen Gay
publicComments.summary: Asked about the rationale for the small boundary cutout near Goodwin and Fernside in Scenario 2 that crosses Alameda, raising safety and contiguity concerns.

publicComments.name: Denise Hannig
publicComments.summary: Argued that children in her neighborhood near Roy Cloud would not need to cross major roads to reach Roy Cloud, making it a safer neighborhood school option than Henry Ford.

publicComments.name: Bill Brown
publicComments.summary: Asked whether there had been any analysis of the impact of boundary changes on PTO funding and potential equity implications, particularly regarding Roy Cloud benefiting at other schools' expense.

publicComments.name: Matt Scott
publicComments.summary: Asked for clarification on whether Nimitz Avenue is a boundary line that would split his neighborhood, and confirmed that under Scenario 1 his side would go to Garfield and under Scenario 2 to Hoover.

publicComments.name: George Lewis
publicComments.summary: Voiced support for Scenario 2, noting Woodside Hills lacks community cohesion and that more neighbors would enroll in RCSD public schools if Scenario 2 were adopted.

publicComments.name: Steve (last name not given)
publicComments.summary: Voiced support for Scenario 2, noting his daughter previously attended Orion and the family is looking for continuity and community at Henry Ford.

publicComments.name: Sarah Yarder
publicComments.summary: Asked whether temperature checks are evidence-based given that many COVID patients don't show fever, and inquired whether the district had considered UVC lamps for classroom disinfection.

publicComments.name: Lily O'Connor
publicComments.summary: Expressed concern about the lack of timely, clear communication from the district, and asked how families with children at different schools on different A/B schedules would coordinate childcare and social circles.

publicComments.name: Abraham Fraley
publicComments.summary: Listed on speaker card but did not appear to speak.

publicComments.name: Michelle Ortez
publicComments.summary: Asked whether teacher survey results would be shared with the board and the public, and when.

publicComments.name: Michelle Smith
publicComments.summary: Recommended that childcare cohorts mirror classroom cohorts to avoid cross-mingling, and offered to connect the district with health literacy research resources to improve community communication.

publicComments.name: Michelle Mulaney and Devin
publicComments.summary: Asked whether contingency plans for more open scenarios had been considered, whether unions had been approached for temporary MoUs to allow volunteers and flexible hours, and whether younger students could receive a greater percentage of in-person time given their greater need for immersion and language acquisition.

publicComments.name: Becky Fouch
publicComments.summary: Asked whether any closed school campuses could be repurposed for childcare or general use to address capacity needs.

publicComments.name: Linda Elkins
publicComments.summary: Expressed surprise that a five-days-per-week option was not included in the parent survey, asked about the district's ability to push back on county guidelines, and noted a survey design flaw that may have limited childcare response data.

publicComments.name: Indra Hernandez
publicComments.summary: A preschool teacher expressed concerns about social distancing being unenforceable with young children, the inadequacy of a two-day in-person model for working parents, and the need for clarity on cleaning responsibilities and job description changes.

publicComments.name: Dina Meyers
publicComments.summary: Praised the district's teachers and asked how they are being supported for the new hybrid model, questioned how to develop curriculum suitable for both in-person and distance-learning/childcare settings, and asked what meaningful social interaction would look like under distancing requirements.

items.title: Discussion of School Plan for Student Achievement
Adoption of Resolution 32, Calling for an Election on November 3, 2020 for the Election of 3 Members of the Governing Board
Approval of Permanently Renaming the 170 Selby Lane Site as Adelante Selby Spanish Immersion School

publicComments.name: Anuj Gagar
publicComments.summary: Urged the board to approve the name Adelante Selby, arguing it has a clear rationale, has twice received a community mandate in votes, and allows the school community to move forward.

publicComments.name: Araceli Tamayo
publicComments.summary: Urged the board to approve Adelante Selby, noting that the combined name honors the traditions and assets of both merged schools and allows alumni of both programs to remain connected.

publicComments.name: Maurice Willis
publicComments.summary: Strongly supported naming the school Adelante Selby, stating that the community has come together around Spanish immersion and that the board should acknowledge this by approving the name.

publicComments.name: Michelle Smith
publicComments.summary: Expressed ongoing frustration with the naming policy process and questioned whether keeping 'Selby' — the name of a wealthy white man — is appropriate for a school dedicated to Spanish immersion and multiculturalism, suggesting 'Unidos' as an alternative.
